items.Sentence: Raw sewage first enters the septage receiving station where it’s mixed with air in the septage holding tanks .
The raw sewage is then received at the headworks, where it’s pas sed through a grit chamber to separate solid particles.

Wastewater is then mixed with activated slu dge in the mixed liquor structure , and it is subsequently directed to a 170 feet (ft) x 124 ft Biolac �� aeration basin where air is once again introduced into the sewage water.

Wastewater discharged from the Biolac �� aeration basin is then passed through two (2) secondary clarifiers (40 ft x 43 ft) in parallel.

Sludge collected from the secondary clarifiers is dewatered at a rotary drum thickener and then pumped to six (6) sludge drying beds (three (3) sludge beds measuring 70 ft x 38 ft and three (3) more measuring 92 ft x 40 ft).

Sludge collected from the secondary clarifiers is dewatered at a rotary drum thickener and then pumped to six (6) sludge drying beds (three (3) sludge beds measuring 70 ft x 38 ft and three (3) more measuring 92 ft x 40 ft).
Leachate collected from the drying beds is pumped b ack to the headworks for reprocessing.
After drying, the sludge is hauled away to a farm in Arizona.
There is an option for the use of a secondary effluent p ump station and continuous backwash upflow filter if deemed necessary by the operational staff.

The wastewater from the secondary clarifiers flows through a ultraviolet (UV) disinfection system and an effluent flow metering system before being discharged to the Pear Drain .
